blocks.md: Homoskedasticity means the scatter of the data around the regression line is about the same everywhere. If you regress food spending on income, the unexplained ups and downs should be as large for low-income households as for high-income ones. Often they are not — richer households vary much more — and that is called heteroskedasticity. It does not move the fitted line on average, but it makes the usual measure of how precise the line is unreliable.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: Getting this wrong produces confidence intervals and test results that look trustworthy but are not, so it decides which standard errors you should report.
If $\mathrm{Var}[e_i\mid x_i]$ depends on $x_i$, the errors are **heteroskedastic**.

sections.heading: What heteroskedasticity does and does not do

blocks.md:
|                                                            | Effect                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Unbiasedness of $b_2$                                      | **Unaffected** — needs only SR1, SR2 ([Strict Exogeneity](note:strict-exogeneity)) and SR5, with random sampling, not SR3 |
| Consistency                                                | Unaffected                                              |
| The usual $\widehat{\sigma}^2/\sum(x_i-\bar{x})^2$ formula | **Wrong** — $t$ stats, $p$ values and intervals invalid |
| [Gauss-Markov Theorem](note:gauss-markov-theorem) / BLUE                            | **Lost** — GLS/WLS is efficient                         |

blocks.md: The lecture's food regression: the residuals spread out as income rises, because richer households have more room to vary their food spending. That fan shape is the usual visual sign of heteroskedasticity; the formal check is the Breusch-Pagan test in [Regression Diagnostics](note:regression-diagnostics).

1. Heteroskedasticity-robust (White) standard errors — keeps OLS, fixes inference
2. Transform the response — [Box-Cox and Power Transformations](note:box-cox-and-power-transformations), logs in particular, when the error scales with the level of $y$
3. Tukey's spread-level plot to find a variance-stabilising power across groups
4. [Bootstrapping OLS](note:bootstrapping-ols) for standard errors without the constant-variance assumption
5. Weighted least squares if the variance function is known

sections.heading: Testing for it and fixing it

blocks.md: Detection: spread-level plots and the Breusch-Pagan, White and Goldfeld-Quandt tests ([Heteroskedasticity Tests](note:heteroskedasticity-tests)); for the food regression all three reject. Remedies: White standard errors ([Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Standard Errors](note:heteroskedasticity-consistent-standard-errors)) keep OLS and fix inference; weighted and feasible generalized least squares ([Generalized Least Squares](note:generalized-least-squares)) restore efficiency.
